request: I want a pair of cable chain links to carry a 6.5 mm cable, printed already assembled with a 0.35 mm gap at the pivot. The cable passes through a 12 x 10 mm opening in each link, 12 mm along the pivot axis and 10 mm across the bend plane. The links should swing 30 degrees in either direction around a vertical pin and then be stopped. Each one is 20 to 40 mm long. They are two separate bodies on the same print and must not touch one another. The pin has a diameter of at least 3.0 mm, and its head covers the bore by at least 0.4 mm per side; there can be at most 0.8 mm of play sideways and at most 1.2 mm along the axis. Lay them flat to print, no supports. Requirements: Deliver two links on one print as separate bodies; each is a single connected piece and they are not joined. State the pivot axis, the straight pose, and how it is oriented for printing. Every link has a straight opening 12 mm in the pivot-axis direction and 10 mm across the bend plane, at least 20 mm long, so that a 6.5 mm cable fits through with at least 0.5 mm to spare. The links are connected by a pivot pin in a bore, with a gap of 0.35 mm around it and 0.35 mm along the axis, so the pin cannot pull out. The pin diameter is at least 3.0 mm, its head overlaps the bore by at least 0.4 mm per side, and play is no more than 0.8 mm sideways and 1.2 mm axially. The pair can swing freely from 30 degrees on one side to 30 degrees on the other, never touching, always at least 0.30 mm apart. A stop halts the bend at 30 degrees on both sides, accurate to one degree. With a 6.5 mm cable running through both inner sections, it stays at least 0.2 mm from both links at every angle from 30 degrees one way to 30 degrees the other. Link length 20 to 40 mm; width across the bend plane no more than 20 mm; height along the pivot axis no more than 25 mm; walls everywhere 1.6 mm or thicker. Both links are printed flat in one run on an FDM printer, with no supports and the pivot axis vertical. The deliverables: an STL of the pair, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout, and the agent's own clearance report, which should agree with an independent measurement.
